question.problem: What is the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={x}^{2}-3x+6\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(4,16)?$
question.worked_solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-3x+6\sqrt{x}) \\  & =2\cdot x-3+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =2x-3+3{x}^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=4$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & =2(4)-3+3(4)^{-1/2} \\  & =8-3+\frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $\frac{13}{2}.$
